note: Thailand from 15 September 2026 (Ministry of Interior announcements in the Royal Gazette of 31 August 2026, ending the 60-day exemption): 30 days without a visa for tourism for the passports of 60 countries and territories, 15 for Seychelles and Mauritius, a visa on arrival for Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia; bilateral agreements give 90 days (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru, Korea), 30 (China, Hong Kong, Kazakhstan, Laos, Macao, Mongolia, Russia, Timor-Leste, Vietnam) or 14 (Cambodia, and Myanmar at international airports only). Business visitors from the 60 need a visa; entries by land on an exemption are limited to two a calendar year (except Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and Singapore): neither is modelled. Everyone else needs a visa.

sources.title: Tourism Authority of Thailand, TAT News: Thailand introduces new 30-day and 15-day visa exemption rules from 15 September (1 September 2026)
sources.said: The related Ministry of Interior announcements were published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026 . ... holders of passports or travel documents from 60 countries and territories will be eligible for visa exemption for tourism, with a permitted stay of up to 30 days . The Royal Gazette lists: Australia Austria Bahrain Belgium Bulgaria Bhutan Brunei Darussalam Canada Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Estonia Fiji Finland France Georgia Germany Greece Hungary Iceland Indonesia India Ireland Israel Italy Japan Jordan Kuwait Kyrgyzstan Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Malta Malaysia Maldives Netherlands New Zealand Norway Oman Philippines Poland Portugal Qatar Romania Saudi Arabia Singapore Slovakia Slovenia South Africa Spain Sweden Switzerland Taiwan Türkiye Ukraine United Arab Emirates United Kingdom United States of America ... A 15-day visa exemption will apply to holders of passports or travel documents from Seychelles and Mauritius . ... Visa on Arrival will apply to holders of passports or travel documents from Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia . Separate bilateral and related entry arrangements will continue to apply where relevant, providing visa exemption periods of 90, 30 or 14 days
